data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported an overall surplus of GBP 5.9 million on prior year reserves in 2020, indicating a release of reserves. This follows a deficit of GBP 1.8 million in 2019. The prior year development reflects a mix of factors, including natural catastrophe loss activity and industry-wide US Casualty reserve deterioration trends, although the syndicate itself did not anticipate adverse development in its own Casualty reserves. The ultimate liability may vary due to subsequent information and events, and adjustments to claims provisions are reflected in the financial statements.
raw_causal_phrases: deterioration of casualty results from previous accident years
estimates of claims subsequently prove to be insufficient (reserving risk)
ultimate liability will vary as a result of subsequent information and events and this may result in significant adjustments to the amounts provided
The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.
Other key circumstances affecting the reliability of assumptions include variation in interest rates, delays in settlement and changes in foreign currency rates.

The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development figure is from explicit narrative statement of 'overall surplus on prior year reserves'. This figure differs from the calculation derived from the gross claims development triangle, which showed a strengthening of +7.305m. The narrative figure is considered more authoritative as it is a direct statement of the overall prior year reserve movement.
